title: Netflix opens 250M-user inventory to Trade Desk buyers, drops spend minimums

facts.fact: Netflix inventory became available to every buyer using The Trade Desk's Sellers and Publishers 500+ marketplace, removing the private-deal requirement, according to the page's report of the July 20, 2026 change.
facts.quote: Netflix inventory today became available to every buyer using The Trade Desk's Sellers and Publishers 500+ marketplace, removing the private-deal requirement

facts.fact: According to The Trade Desk, buyers can reach Netflix inventory through Sellers and Publishers 500+ with no minimum spend and no change to their workflow.
facts.quote: no minimum spend or change to your workflow required to reach Netflix inventory.

facts.fact: According to The Trade Desk, the Netflix inclusion gives buyers access to Netflix's more than 250 million global monthly active users.
facts.quote: the inclusion gives buyers access to Netflix's more than 250 million global monthly active users

facts.fact: Netflix presented a global monthly ad-supported reach of 250 million viewers at its 2026 advertising upfront on May 13, 2026.
facts.quote: Netflix itself presented at its 2026 advertising upfront on May 13, 2026

facts.fact: The 250 million Netflix audience figure counts individual viewers within ad-supported households rather than subscriber accounts, according to the page.
facts.quote: The 250 million figure represents individual viewers within ad-supported households rather than subscriber accounts

facts.fact: Netflix was chasing roughly $3 billion in advertising revenue for 2026, nearly double the approximately $1.5 billion it generated in 2025.
facts.unit: billion USD (2026 target); approx. 1.5 billion USD (2025)
facts.quote: Netflix has spent 2026 chasing roughly $3 billion in advertising revenue for the year, nearly double the approximately $1.5 billion it generated in 2025.

facts.fact: Netflix told investors on its first-quarter 2026 earnings call that programmatic buying was on course to become more than 50 percent of its non-live advertising business.
facts.quote: programmatic buying was on course to become more than 50 percent of its

facts.fact: Amazon's ad sales fees are roughly 1 percent, which the page contrasts with a 12 to 15 percent range that investment bank Needham and Co. attributed to The Trade Desk.
facts.unit: % ad sales fee (Amazon); 12-15% (Needham estimate for The Trade Desk)
facts.quote: its ad sales fees of roughly 1 percent standing far below the

facts.fact: In August 2024, Netflix reported a 150 percent increase in upfront commitments compared with 2023.
facts.quote: In August 2024, Netflix reported a 150 percent increase in upfront commitments compared with 2023

facts.fact: A July 2025 EMEA targeting release added mood targeting, postal-code precision, and more than 100 interest segments for Netflix ads.
facts.quote: brought mood targeting, postal-code precision, and more than 100 interest segments.

facts.fact: Netflix added Yahoo DSP as a fourth global programmatic partner in June 2025.
facts.quote: The company added Yahoo DSP as a fourth global programmatic partner in June 2025

facts.fact: Netflix reported that new programmatic access to Pause Ads and live sports inventory was arriving in summer 2026.
facts.quote: the company flagged new programmatic access to Pause Ads and live sports inventory as arriving this summer.
